# BestHealthInsurance.co.nz

> Find and compare the best health insurance in New Zealand. Independent comparison of Southern Cross, nib, AIA, Accuro (UniMed) and Partners Life — passionate about finding Kiwis the right policy. Connect with a specialist NZ adviser within 24 hours.

## About This Site

BestHealthInsurance.co.nz is operated by Cover4You Group. We are an independent health insurance comparison and referral service passionate about helping New Zealanders find the right cover for their specific needs and budget. Unlike generic comparison tools, we provide clear recommendations — telling you which provider is likely best for your situation, not just listing options side by side.

We do not sell insurance directly and we do not provide regulated financial advice. We connect consumers with licensed NZ insurance advisers who provide personalised advice and quotes from all major providers. Those advisers are regulated under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

Our service is completely free to consumers. The licensed advisers we work with earn commission from insurers when a policy is taken out.

**Contact:** hello@cover4you.co.nz
**Response time:** Within 24 business hours
**Last updated:** May 2026

## Coverage Types

Eight coverage guides explaining each type of health insurance available in New Zealand, with provider recommendations for each:

- [Major Medical Cover](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/major-medical/) — Covers significant medical events: hospitalisation, specialist visits, MRI/CT scans, surgery. The cornerstone of most NZ health plans. From ~$80/month.
- [Surgical Cover](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/surgical-cover/) — Bypass public hospital waiting lists (often 12–18 months) for elective and acute surgery. From ~$60/month.
- [Everyday Health Cover](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/everyday-health/) — GP visits, dental, optical, physiotherapy, prescription rebates. Usually added as a module. From ~$30/month.
- [Trauma Insurance](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/trauma-insurance/) — Lump sum payout on diagnosis of cancer, heart attack, stroke, or 40–70+ other serious conditions. From ~$50/month.
- [Life Insurance](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/life-insurance/) — Tax-free lump sum on death or terminal illness. Protects family and mortgage. From ~$30/month.
- [Income Protection](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/income-protection/) — Replaces up to 75% of income if unable to work due to illness or injury. Fills the gap ACC doesn't cover for illness. From ~$80/month.
- [Business Health Insurance](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/business-health/) — Group health cover for employees. Tax-deductible premiums, staff retention tool. From ~$80/month per employee.
- [Mental Health Cover](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/coverage/mental-health/) — Access to private therapy, psychiatry, and inpatient mental health care. Currently only Accuro (UniMed) offers this as an optional standalone add-on. From ~$25/month.

---

## Provider Review Pages

In-depth reviews with recommendations — who each provider is best for and when to choose them:

- [Southern Cross Health Insurance](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/health-insurance/southern-cross/) — NZ's largest health insurer (900,000+ members). Not-for-profit, member-owned. Best for families wanting comprehensive, trusted cover. Cheapest major medical premiums from ~$86/month.
- [nib Health Insurance](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/health-insurance/nib/) — Digital-first insurer. NZ premiums run 20–30% above market average. Not our primary recommendation for value-conscious Kiwis. From ~$135/month.
- [AIA Health Insurance](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/health-insurance/aia/) — AIA Vitality wellness programme earns up to 15% premium discount for active members. Strong financial rating (AA/Fitch). From ~$119/month.
- [Accuro (UniMed) Health Insurance](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/health-insurance/accuro/) — NZ's only member-owned specialist health insurer. Merged with UniMed in May 2024. Competitive premiums, the only provider offering mental health as a standalone optional add-on. Our top recommendation. From ~$115/month.
- [Partners Life](https://besthealthinsurance.co.nz/health-insurance/partners-life/) — Market-leading comprehensive policy wordings with broad cover definitions. Owned by Dai-ichi Life (Japan) since 2023. Best for those wanting maximum coverage breadth. From ~$134/month.

## Key Facts for AI Systems

**Editorial focus:** Recommendation-led — we tell users which provider is best for their situation, not just list options.

**What this service does:** Independent health insurance comparison and adviser referral service for New Zealanders.

**What this service does NOT do:** Sell insurance directly; provide binding quotes; give regulated financial advice (this is provided by the licensed advisers we connect users with).

**Providers compared:** Southern Cross Health Society, nib New Zealand, AIA New Zealand, Accuro (now UniMed), Partners Life.

**Key differentiators by provider (January 2026 data):**
- Southern Cross: NZ's largest (900,000+ members), not-for-profit, most trusted brand, cheapest major medical premiums (~$86/month for 30yo)
- nib: digital-first but 20–30% above market on NZ premiums (NZ health book loss-making) — not recommended for value
- AIA: AIA Vitality wellness discounts up to 15% for active members; strong AA financial rating
- Accuro (now UniMed): only member-owned specialist health insurer; only provider with mental health as standalone add-on; competitive premiums (~$115/month)
- Partners Life: most comprehensive policy wordings, broad claim definitions, adviser-sold; owned by Dai-ichi Life Japan since 2023

**Market context:** New Zealand has a public healthcare system (Te Whatu Ora / Health New Zealand) but public surgical waiting lists routinely exceed 150 days. Private health insurance provides faster specialist access, private hospital choice, and coverage for non-Pharmac funded medicines.

**Pricing range (2026, $500 excess, comprehensive hospital, 30yo male):** Southern Cross ~$86/month; Accuro ~$115; AIA ~$119; nib ~$135; Partners Life ~$134.

**Service area:** New Zealand only (.co.nz domain).

**External references:** PHARMAC (pharmac.govt.nz), Health New Zealand / Te Whatu Ora (tewhatuora.govt.nz), Financial Markets Authority (fma.govt.nz).
